title: BatchNorm vs LayerNorm
interviewAnswer: BatchNorm normalizes using batch statistics and is common in CNNs; LayerNorm normalizes features within each example and is standard in transformers. Their behavior at inference differs.
why: BatchNorm vs LayerNorm is a common deep-learning question because they normalize along different dimensions and behave differently in training/inference.
intuition: BatchNorm uses statistics across examples for each feature/channel. LayerNorm uses statistics within each example across its hidden features.
deepDive: BatchNorm normalizes activations using batch mean/variance and maintains running estimates for inference; small/non-iid batches can make estimates noisy. LayerNorm normalizes per token/sample and does not depend on other examples, making it natural for transformers and variable sequence lengths. Both include learned scale/shift parameters; neither simply “forces mean 0 forever.”
math:
BN: x̂=(x-μ_batch)/sqrt(σ²_batch+ε); y=γx̂+β
LN: same form but μ,σ computed across chosen feature dimensions per sample
workedExample: A transformer token of dimension 768 can be LayerNormed across those 768 features independently of batch size, while BatchNorm would couple it to other batch examples.
commonMistakes: Saying BatchNorm uses the current batch at inference.
Saying LayerNorm normalizes across the batch.
production: Ensure training/eval modes are correct and saved running statistics are loaded. Distribution shifts can make BatchNorm statistics less representative.

visual.caption: Normalization stabilizes activation scales; BatchNorm and LayerNorm normalize along different axes.
